key_insight: A variationally correct first-order least-squares residual makes physics-informed operator learning locally error-equivalent in the PDE-compliant norm.
engineering_relevance: For nonlinear mechanics, including compressible Neo-Hookean hyperelasticity, this provides a principled training objective and an inference-time error indicator.
method: Establish residual–error equivalence using linearized stability and Lipschitz continuity of the residual derivative.
Train a reduced-basis neural operator in a conforming finite element space, using solution snapshots only to construct the basis.
Assemble the residual loss and its symbolically derived gradient with a finite element library.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests show that the square root of loss excess tracks error within factors comparable to the linear case, while the operator outperforms grid-based baselines in the PDE-compliant norm.
watch_item: The guarantees depend on stability and regularity assumptions and may hold only near a solution branch, rather than globally.
paper_title: Variationally correct physics-informed operator learning for nonlinear partial differential equations
